findings.evidence: "Similarly, the IT asset group tracks the equipment catalog on the first business day of the month."
findings.violation: "Similarly" is incorrect - one update happens at the fiscal year start, the other monthly; these operations are not parallel.

findings.evidence: "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.fix: Specify: "The annual benefit year clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.violation: "The stipend clock" is ambiguous - it could refer to either the 90-day eligibility requirement or the annual benefit year clock.

findings.evidence: "an incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives"
findings.fix: Change to "until the missing information is provided."
findings.violation: The phrase "missing item arrives" is incorrect; this describes incomplete REQUEST information, not missing physical items.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests. Additionally, employees must retain receipts for one year after the purchase date."
findings.fix: Clarify: "Employees must retain either the original receipt or a photo for one year after the purchase date."
findings.violation: It is unclear whether "retain receipts" means keep original receipts, photos, or both, especially after the previous sentence allows photos for most requests.

findings.evidence: "The finance office deposits the amount within one pay cycle."
findings.fix: Specify: "The finance office deposits the approved reimbursement amount within one pay cycle."
findings.violation: "The amount" is ambiguous - unclear whether this means the full $500 stipend, the approved amount, or the requested amount.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite as "Employees must keep their equipment in good working condition, and the benefits team may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.violation: This uses inconsistent point of view (second person "You" and first person plural "we") when the rest of the document uses third person ("employees," "the manager," etc.).

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee."
findings.fix: Replace "Similarly," with "Additionally," or "The policy also applies to."
findings.violation: "Similarly" incorrectly suggests this device restriction is parallel to the equipment maintenance requirement above it.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form... Also, you submit the request in the portal. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Rewrite using third person: "Employees record the stipend item on the request form... Employees submit the request in the portal. Employees track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.violation: This section uses inconsistent point of view with second person "You" when the rest of the document uses third person throughout.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review."
findings.fix: Use clearer terminology: "Employees record each equipment purchase on the request form. Finance reconciles each purchase against the request log each month. Payroll releases the reimbursement amount after that monthly review."
findings.violation: The term "stipend item" is used repeatedly and lacks clarity about what it refers to - the individual equipment purchase, a line item on the form, or the dollar amount.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Clarify scope: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility and uploading the receipt; the request then proceeds to manager and finance reviews."
findings.violation: Only two steps are listed, yet earlier sections describe additional steps including manager review and finance review for requests over $200, making this incomplete or incorrectly simplified.

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison publishes the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year. Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Either rename the section to "Catalog Management" or replace with actual special cases if they exist.
findings.violation: The section title "Special Cases" does not match the content, which describes catalog management procedures rather than any special cases or exceptions.

findings.evidence: "The finance office also flags any request that repeats within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Specify the condition: "The finance office also flags any request from the same employee within the same quarter."
findings.violation: "Repeats" is vague and unclear - could mean a repeat from the same employee, same equipment type, same amount, or a resubmitted request.

findings.evidence: "The manager reviews the request within two business days... The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out."
findings.fix: Clarify the relationship: "In addition to manager approval, the finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out."
findings.violation: It is unclear whether the finance office review occurs in addition to or instead of the manager review, creating ambiguity in the approval workflow.

findings.evidence: "The benefits team reviews the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year."
findings.fix: Remove this sentence or consolidate all equipment catalog information into a single document location.
findings.violation: This information is already stated in earlier sections (Program Overview and Special Cases), creating redundant content.

findings.evidence: Section heading "Questions and Updates" followed by content about reviewing equipment catalogs and requesting printed copies.
findings.fix: Rename the section to "Equipment Catalog Access" or "Documentation and Support."
findings.violation: The section title does not match the content, which is about equipment catalog access rather than questions or updates.
